The documentation describes the algorithm in detail but does not report a testbench or silicon results, and no external hardware is specified. results.summary: This design is a compact spiking neural network heart-beat classifier for Tiny Tapeout. It accepts 12-bit ADC samples on the input pins and uses a heartbeat segmenter, delta encoder, a five-neuron parallel SNN matrix, and a multi-class voter to classify beats into AAMI-style classes. An alarm output asserts after three consecutive anomaly classifications, and a diagnostic-valid output pulses when a class result is available. The documentation describes a cocotb test suite including an MIT-BIH stream excerpt, but no silicon results are reported.

results.summary: This project is an S/PDIF (AES3 consumer) receiver that converts an incoming digital-audio stream into an I2S master output. It recovers timing from the incoming biphase-mark-coded stream using only the free-running Tiny Tapeout clock, with no external audio clock or PLL. The design also includes an analog comparator intended for off-chip mute-delay hysteresis, and a 1-bit PWM mono audio output. A self-checking testbench with a behavioural S/PDIF encoder and I2S decoder is provided, but no silicon results are reported.

results.summary: This design converts an SPI-style APA102 LED protocol stream into a single-line WS2812 output. It is hard-coded for seven LEDs, waits for a 32-bit low start condition, shifts in the pixel data, and forwards it to the WS2812 output until a stop condition is recognized. It ignores the APA102 intensity byte and also emits a continuous UART output of "Arglius Barglius" at approximately 115200 baud. Testing requires an SPI driver and a string of at least seven WS2812 LEDs, and no silicon results are reported.

results.summary_before: This Wokwi project implements an 8-bit linear-feedback shift register that acts as a pseudo-random number generator. It uses a shift-register structure with feedback to produce a sequence of random-looking bits. The output is displayed on LEDs, and the design is controlled by switches. It is a simple educational example of LFSR-based PRNG.
results.summary: This design contains two numerically controlled oscillators implemented with phase accumulators and sine lookup tables. Their outputs are multiplied together by default, and NCO B can be bypassed to a constant one or half. A boxcar filter is also included, and at 50 MHz NCO A can be tuned from about 24.8 MHz down to 0.195 MHz while NCO B reaches up to 12.3 MHz. The output is intended for an R-2R DAC and an oscilloscope, and no silicon results are reported.

results.summary: This project is an experiment with Deep Differential Logic Networks for classifying hand-written MNIST digits at 16x16 pixels. It accepts an 8-bit input packet shifted in on the input pins and outputs a 4-bit digit plus a 7-bit confidence score. A /WE input pauses the design, and an external MCU is needed to provide input data and read out results. The documentation is sparse and the test procedure is still marked TO DO, with no silicon results reported.
